title: Canada EI regular beneficiaries, August 2026
question: What will Statistics Canada first report for Canada's seasonally adjusted regular Employment Insurance beneficiaries in August 2026, expressed in thousands?
resolutionRule: Resolve using the first official published August 2026 observation for vector v64549350 in Statistics Canada Table 14-10-0011-01: Canada, regular Employment Insurance beneficiaries, seasonally adjusted, persons. Multiply the published value by 0.001 to express it in thousands, preserving its published precision. Exclude all subsequent revisions and corrections.
drivers: Persistence of the July beneficiary stock
August employment losses with unchanged unemployment
Existing EI access and duration measures
Claim processing, benefit exhaustion and seasonal revisions

reasoning.text: August EI beneficiaries: persistence with a small upward adjustment

Extended WDS and customized-table requests failed, so a consistent current-vintage history longer than five months could not be fetched. The seven release-headline observations provide the reference class; their successive changes include revisions between releases.

The outside-view base rate is persistence near July's 547.05 thousand. Across the seven January–July release headlines, the mean level is 546.011 thousand and the mean successive change is -1.297 thousand. Recent April–July movement instead averages +0.87 thousand per month, supporting only a small, shrunk momentum adjustment.

reasoning.result: Seasonally adjusted employment declined 42,000 (-0.2%) to 21,173,000. Unemployment remained 6.4%; participation fell 0.1 percentage points to 65.0%. Public-sector employment declined 20,000. The explicitly unadjusted layoff rate was 0.8%, compared with 1.0% in August 2025.

The normal 1-week waiting period is waived for claims starting March 30, 2025–October 9, 2027, and separation-earnings allocation is suspended over that span. Eligible long-tenured workers receive 20 additional regular-benefit weeks, up to 65, for claims starting June 15, 2025–June 12, 2027. The latest-separation review measure begins October 11, 2026.

reasoning.text: Level: July's stock is the anchor. Momentum: retain half the recent average increase. One-off effects: August employment losses suggest modest additional inflows, tempered by unchanged unemployment, lower participation and subdued layoffs. Policy mechanism: access and duration measures already operate in the historical sample, so assign no separate policy increment. The October eligibility change does not apply to August.

Prior/update/interval: Use a one-month persistence prior with shrunk recent drift, based on seven fetched January–July release headlines. Start at 547.05 thousand; add momentum of 0.5*((547.05-544.44)/3) = 0.435 thousand and a judgmental labour-market adjustment of 0.5 thousand; add zero separate policy or identified one-off adjustment. Round 547.985 to 548.0 thousand. Successive changes are [-12.72, 5.89, -3.56, -0.75, -1.73, 5.09] thousand; sigma = 6.760762 thousand, calculated as sqrt(228.539533/5). A Gaussian 80% interval has half-width 1.28*sigma = 8.653776 thousand, rounded to 8.65, implying bounds 539.35–556.65 thousand. No further widening or narrowing is applied; release-headline dispersion already includes intervening revision effects.

Upside risk: stronger eligible inflows from public-sector separations, delayed claim processing or slower exits could lift beneficiaries above 556.65 thousand. Downside risk: faster reemployment or concentrated benefit exhaustion could push beneficiaries below 539.35 thousand. An unusually large seasonal or administrative revision accompanying the first release could also put the result outside the interval.
